Problems   with   NSW: 
•   poly-logarithmic   search   complexity 
•   “traf fi c   hubs”/high   out-degrees   vertices 
ANN   index:   HNSW   (Hierarchical   Navigable   Small   World) 
stacking   up   NSWs 
Hierarchical   NSW   (HNSW): 
•   stack   multiple   NSWs   into   a   hierarchical   structure 
-   layer   0:   NSW   of   ,   layer   1:   NSW   of   c%-D,   … 
-   upper   layer:   larger   distance   scale 
•   bound   average   degree 
-   avoid   adding   an   edge   that   forms   the   longest   edge   of   a   triangle

ANN   index:   HNSW   (Hierarchical   Navigable   Small   World) 
stacking   up   NSWs 
Query   with   HNSW   (for   query   vector   ): 
•   start   with   a   pre-de fi ned   “entry”   vertex   as   the   current   vertex   in   the   top   layer 
•   use   Greedy   to   fi nd   closest   neighbor   of   the   current   vertex   at   the   layer 
•   use   as   the   current   vertex   in   the   layer   one   level   below,   and   go   to   the   last   step 
•   repeat   until   layer   0   is   reached,   and   search   top-k   results   via   Greedy

How   does   LSM-tree   achieve   these,   conceptually? 
buffer   writes   in-memory   (MemTable) 
fl ash   MemTable   periodically   to   disk   as   a   segment 
merge   segments   periodically   into   larger   ones 
Log   Structured   Merge   Tree   (LSM-tree) 
avoid   frequently   random   writes 
fl exible   trade-off:   read   ef fi ciency   &   consistency 
Three   types   of   disk   writes 
-   write-ahead-log   (WAL) 
-   compaction 
-   metadata   update   (LSM   index) 
[Mei   et   al.   SoCC’17]

Read   in   LSM-tree 
starting   from   MemTable 
look   for   read   key   through   levels   (optimized   via   BloomFilter) 
Deletion   in   LSM-tree 
logically   deleted   by   inserting   tombstones ,   a   special   key-value   entry 
deletions   are   physically   “implemented”   during   compaction

search:   slow-writeable   fast-readable   structure   (SWFR) 
Reconcile   FWSR   into   SWFR   at   a   convenient   time 
index   update   in   Milvus   (credit:   Pan   et   al.   SIGMOD’24   tutorial)

-   build   per-seg   HNSW 
-   reconcile   tombstones 
-   index   merger   [SingleStore-V] 
-   snapshot   isolation 
can replace HNSW with other index

Quantisation: 
aim:   reduce   the   size   of   vectors   (and   consequently,   their   indices) 
idea:   bin   (groups   of)   dimensions’   values   separately   into   discrete   buckets 
d   dimensions 
v 1   v 2   … 
PCA:   reduce   height   ( ) 
quantisation:   reduce   width 
d 
32* d   bits 
k-means   as   a   quantiser: 
all   vectors   in   a   cluster   are   encoded   by   the   same   centroid 
replace   centroid   vectors   with   centroid   IDs 
codebook :   map   centroid   IDs   to   centroid   vectors 
intended application of Lloyd's algorithm in 1957 at Bell Labs 
size   reduction:   (of   size   )   vs   codebook   (of   size   )   + D   nd   kd   k   log2   k

=== PDF PAGE 57 ===
Product   quantisation: 
partition   vectors   into   subvectors 
quantise   subvectors   independently   via   k-means 
concatenate   centroid   IDs   into   compressed   (quantised)   vectors 
can   be   incorporated   into   vector   index,   e.g.,   IVF-PQ 
credit:   https://zilliz.com/learn/scalar-quantization-and-product-quantization
